subject: physics
title: The Big Bang and Steady State theories
key_idea: The Big Bang theory says the Universe began from a very small, extremely hot, dense region and is expanding. The Steady State theory says it has no beginning and new matter forms continually. Red-shift and CMB radiation support the Big Bang, which is the accepted model.

sections.heading: Two theories of the origin of the Universe

blocks.text: (Physics only, not needed for Combined Science) The Big Bang and Steady State theories are two models for how the Universe began and how it has changed.

items.meaning: The Universe began from a very small region that was extremely hot and dense, and has been expanding since.
The Universe has no beginning. It is expanding, and new matter forms continually.
Cosmic microwave background radiation: microwave radiation detected from all over the sky.

diagram.alt: The Big Bang theory and the Steady State theory compared.

values: No continual formation of new matter

items: Both theories say the Universe is expanding.
The Big Bang has a beginning. The Steady State has none, and needs new matter to form continually.

blocks.text: Evidence decides which theory scientists accept.

items: **Red-shift** shows distant galaxies are moving away, so the Universe is expanding. Both theories account for this.
The increase of speed with distance, followed backwards, points to a beginning at a single point.
**CMB radiation** is microwave radiation left over from the beginning. It is detected from all over the sky.
The radiation is microwaves because of cooling. A typical wavelength is about 1 mm.
The Big Bang theory has more evidence supporting it than the Steady State theory, so it is the currently accepted model.

diagram.alt: Sort the evidence by which theory it supports.
diagram.prompt: Which theory does each piece of evidence support?
groups: Supports the Big Bang over Steady State

items.text: Galaxies are moving away from us
Microwave radiation is detected from all over the sky
Radiation left over from an initial explosion is still present

items: Red-shift supports expansion, and both theories account for it.
The discovery of CMB radiation led to the Big Bang becoming the accepted model.

blocks.text: Scientists change theories when new observations do not fit the current model.

items: The Big Bang model first suggested that gravity would slow the rate at which galaxies move apart.
Since 1998, observations suggest that distant galaxies are moving away at an increasingly fast rate.
There is still much about the Universe that is not understood, such as dark mass and dark energy.
New evidence that does not fit a theory leads scientists to change it.
Observations of supernovae suggest the expansion is speeding up.

checks.q: Give one similarity and one difference between the Big Bang theory and the Steady State theory.
checks.a: Similarity: both say the Universe is expanding. Difference: the Steady State theory has no beginning and needs continual formation of new matter, but the Big Bang theory has a beginning.

checks.q: Explain how the presence of CMB radiation provides evidence for the Big Bang theory.
checks.a: The Big Bang theory has a beginning or initial explosion. This released radiation, which is still present.

checks.q: Explain why the Big Bang theory is the currently accepted model.
checks.a: More evidence supports the Big Bang theory than the Steady State theory, including red-shift and the discovery of CMB radiation.

exam_phrases: expanding at an ever greater rate
new observations / evidence that does not fit into the current theory / model

mistakes.wrong: The Big Bang theory says the Universe began very small.
mistakes.right: 'Very small' is ignored on its own. Describe the early Universe as extremely hot and dense.

mistakes.wrong: New observations suggest the expansion of the Universe is slowing down.
mistakes.right: The new observations suggest distant galaxies are moving away at an increasingly fast rate: expanding at an ever greater rate.

worked_example.question:
The Big Bang theory is one model used to explain the origin of the universe.

How does the Big Bang theory describe the universe when it began?
worked_example.tip: 'Very small' is ignored on its own.

exam_phrases: the Steady State theory has no beginning
the Steady State theory requires the continual formation of new matter
the Big Bang theory has a beginning / initial explosion
microwave radiation left over from the beginning
detected from all over the sky

mistakes.wrong: Both theories say the Universe had a beginning.
mistakes.right: Only the Big Bang has a beginning. The similarity is that both have an expanding Universe.

mistakes.wrong: CMB radiation shows the Universe is expanding.
mistakes.right: Red-shift shows expansion. CMB radiation is evidence for the Big Bang because the initial explosion released radiation that is still present.

worked_example.question:
The Big Bang theory gives an explanation for the origin of the Universe.

Explain how evidence supports the ideas that
● the Universe is expanding
● the Universe began at a single point.
answer_points: Expansion: light from distant galaxies is red-shifted, so its observed wavelength is longer.
This shows the sources are moving away. (Nearly) all galaxies show this, an example of the Doppler effect.
Beginning at a point: the increase of recessional velocities with distance, extrapolated back.
CMB radiation is microwave radiation left over from the beginning.
It is microwaves because of cooling, and is detected from all over the sky.
worked_example.tip: A six-mark level-marked answer. Higher levels need accurate, detailed and logically structured physics for both ideas.

exam_phrases: the Big Bang is a model of how the Universe began
the light has a longer wavelength when it reaches Earth than when it was emitted
distant galaxies are moving away faster so the Universe is expanding

mistakes.wrong: Distant galaxies are moving away faster, so the Universe is contracting.
mistakes.right: Galaxies moving apart means the Universe is expanding.

mistakes.wrong: Light from distant galaxies has a longer wavelength. This is called CMBR.
mistakes.right: An increase in wavelength of light from galaxies is called red shift. CMBR is the radiation left over from the Big Bang.
